regulatory_authority.value: Oregon Health Authority, Oregon Psilocybin Services Section

legal_basis.value: ORS chapter 475A (Oregon Psilocybin Services Act, Ballot Measure 109, 2020): OHA licenses manufacturers, service centers, facilitators and laboratories; clients 21+; administration sessions only at licensed service centers. Psilocybin remains federally Schedule I.

access_pathway_details.text: Psilocybin services are provided at licensed psilocybin service centers under ORS 475A (Ballot Measure 109). Adults 21+ can access services without a prescription or medical referral. A preparation session with a licensed facilitator is required before an administration session, which must take place at a service center; facilitators follow up within 72 hours and offer integration sessions.

eligibility_requirements.text: Must be 21 or older. Oregon residency is not required, and no prescription, medical referral or diagnosis is required. Facilitators may decline services, and certain answers on the Client Information Form can make a client ineligible.

provider_requirements.text: Facilitators must hold an OHA facilitator license (age 21+, high school diploma or equivalent, OHA-approved training, and a passed examination); OHA may not require a degree. Administration sessions must be held at a licensed psilocybin service center. Products are tested by licensed laboratories that must first be ORELAP-accredited.

residency_travel_notes.text: No residency requirement: clients do not need to live in Oregon. Psilocybin can only be purchased and consumed at a licensed service center during an administration session; products may not be taken off-site, and clients stay a minimum time based on dose.

risk_notes.text: Products are tested for species identity and psilocybin potency; testing for microbials, heavy metals or pesticides is at OPS's discretion rather than routine. Facilitators may decline services, and some answers on the Client Information Form can make a client ineligible.

oversight_notes.text: The Oregon Health Authority's Oregon Psilocybin Services Section licenses and regulates manufacturers, service centers, facilitators and laboratories under ORS 475A. Laboratories test products for Psilocybe cubensis identity and psilocybin potency.

cost_notes.text: Prices are set by each service center and facilitator; Oregon Psilocybin Services does not set or regulate the costs of psilocybin products or services.

arbitrage_summary.text: State-licensed psilocybin services open to adults 21+ without a prescription, referral or Oregon residency. Psilocybin remains Schedule I under federal law.

regulatory_authority.value: Health Canada (Special Access Program; Office of Controlled Substances)

legal_basis.value: Controlled Drugs and Substances Act: production, sale and possession of psilocybin are illegal unless authorized by Health Canada. Psilocybin is a restricted drug obtainable for individual patients through the Special Access Program (serious or life-threatening conditions where conventional treatments have failed, are unsuitable or unavailable) or individual subsection 56(1) CDSA exemptions. No approved psilocybin product.

access_pathway_details.text: Practitioners can request psilocybin for an individual patient through Health Canada's Special Access Program when the patient has a serious or life-threatening condition and conventional treatments have failed, are unsuitable or unavailable. Individual subsection 56(1) CDSA exemptions are another route, generally only where clinical trials or the SAP are not possible or suitable. No psilocybin product is approved in Canada.

eligibility_requirements.text: Serious or life-threatening condition for which conventional treatments have failed, are unsuitable or unavailable; the request is made by the treating practitioner on a patient-specific form.

provider_requirements.text: The requesting practitioner must be licensed to prescribe in their province or territory. The drug must come from a licensed dealer, and imported product needs a Health Canada import permit.

risk_notes.text: An SAP authorization is not a Health Canada finding that the drug is safe or effective.

oversight_notes.text: Health Canada reviews each SAP request case by case. A subsection 56(1) class exemption lets practitioners, pharmacists, hospitals and licensed dealers handle SAP-authorized psilocybin; Health Canada states it will be revoked when new Controlled Substances Regulations take effect on 1 October 2026.

arbitrage_summary.text: Case-by-case federal access through the Special Access Program or a subsection 56(1) exemption for patients with serious conditions; not an open or commercial market.

access_pathway_details.text: Same Oregon psilocybin services pathway as for any adult client: services at licensed service centers under ORS 475A, with no prescription, medical referral or diagnosis required, so adults 21+ may seek services for end-of-life distress. A preparation session precedes the administration session, which must take place at a service center.

eligibility_requirements.text: Must be 21 or older; no prescription, medical referral or terminal diagnosis is required; Oregon residency is not required. Facilitators may decline services.

provider_requirements.text: Facilitators must hold an OHA facilitator license (age 21+, high school diploma or equivalent, OHA-approved training, and a passed examination); OHA may not require a degree. Administration sessions must be held at a licensed psilocybin service center. Products are tested by licensed laboratories that must first be ORELAP-accredited.

residency_travel_notes.text: No residency requirement: clients do not need to live in Oregon. Psilocybin can only be purchased and consumed at a licensed service center during an administration session; products may not be taken off-site, and clients stay a minimum time based on dose.

risk_notes.text: Products are tested for species identity and psilocybin potency; testing for microbials, heavy metals or pesticides is at OPS's discretion rather than routine. Facilitators may decline services, and some answers on the Client Information Form can make a client ineligible.

oversight_notes.text: The Oregon Health Authority's Oregon Psilocybin Services Section licenses and regulates manufacturers, service centers, facilitators and laboratories under ORS 475A. Laboratories test products for Psilocybe cubensis identity and psilocybin potency.

cost_notes.text: Prices are set by each service center and facilitator; Oregon Psilocybin Services does not set or regulate the costs of psilocybin products or services.

arbitrage_summary.text: Adults 21+ can access state-licensed psilocybin services without a diagnosis, prescription, referral or Oregon residency. Psilocybin remains federally Schedule I.

legal_basis.value: Controlled Drugs and Substances Act: production, sale and possession of psilocybin are illegal unless authorized by Health Canada. Psilocybin is a restricted drug obtainable for individual patients through the Special Access Program (serious or life-threatening conditions where conventional treatments have failed, are unsuitable or unavailable) or individual subsection 56(1) CDSA exemptions. No approved psilocybin product.

access_pathway_details.text: Psilocybin for end-of-life distress can be requested case by case: Practitioners can request psilocybin for an individual patient through Health Canada's Special Access Program when the patient has a serious or life-threatening condition and conventional treatments have failed, are unsuitable or unavailable. Individual subsection 56(1) CDSA exemptions are another route, generally only where clinical trials or the SAP are not possible or suitable. No psilocybin product is approved in Canada.

eligibility_requirements.text: Serious or life-threatening condition for which conventional treatments have failed, are unsuitable or unavailable; the request is made by the treating practitioner on a patient-specific form.

provider_requirements.text: The requesting practitioner must be licensed to prescribe in their province or territory. The drug must come from a licensed dealer, and imported product needs a Health Canada import permit.

risk_notes.text: An SAP authorization is not a Health Canada finding that the drug is safe or effective.

oversight_notes.text: Health Canada reviews each SAP request case by case. A subsection 56(1) class exemption lets practitioners, pharmacists, hospitals and licensed dealers handle SAP-authorized psilocybin; Health Canada states it will be revoked when new Controlled Substances Regulations take effect on 1 October 2026.

arbitrage_summary.text: Case-by-case federal access through the Special Access Program or a subsection 56(1) exemption for patients with serious conditions; not an open or commercial market.
